I fixed the bug: the `` example from the report now renders as a single paragraph with the comment kept in place. **Cause:** in `markdown/htmlparser.py`, a comment at the start of a line was always treated as a standalone raw HTML block. That ended the current paragraph (`

`) and started a new one after the comment (`

`), even when the comment sat inside an inline element like `` that hadn't been closed yet. **Fix:** - `HTMLExtractor` now keeps a list of inline tags that are open in the current paragraph. Self-closing tags like `` and `` are skipped. A closing tag removes its entry, and a blank line or a new raw block clears the list. - A comment (or another block-level empty tag) is treated as a standalone block only when no inline tag is open; otherwise it stays inside the paragraph. - The `md_in_html` extension handles inline tags in its own code, so I added the same tracking there through three small helpers (`push_inline_tag`, `pop_inline_tag`, `check_inline_data`). **Unchanged:** a comment on its own line still splits a paragraph when nothing inline is open, e.g. `para\n\nmore`, or after `x`. **Tests:** I added three regression tests to `tests/test_syntax/blocks/test_html_blocks.py` and one to `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_md_in_html.py`. Result: 1040 passed, 110 skipped. To get a clean run I had to work around two problems with this environment, not the code: - `tests/test_apis.py` needs `yaml`, which isn't installed, so I left it out. - The extensions aren't registered in the venv, so names like `md_in_html` can't be found. For the test run only, I mapped those names to `markdown.extensions.`. Without that, the `md_in_html` tests fail with `ModuleNotFoundError` whether or not my change is applied. pytest also can't collect a helper class called `TestSuite` in `test_md_in_html.py`; that error comes from the test setup, not from this change. One limitation: a tag name written inside a code span on the same paragraph, such as `` `` ``, also counts as an open tag. A comment later in that paragraph would then stay inline instead of becoming its own block.
